**Step length model** (2): transformed response s̃_ijt (scaled arcsin of min-max-normalized step length) ~ N(μ^(SL)_ijt, σ²), μ^(SL)_ijt = α^(SL)_0 + X^(SL)_ijt β^(SL) + u_j + v_k; ball-carrier random intercept u_j ~ N(0, τ²_u), defensive-team random intercept v_k ~ N(0, τ²_v); covariates = ball carrier + closest defender features, player counts per direction, and previous-frame step length.

**Turn angle model** (3): φ_ijt ~ von Mises(μ^(TA)_ijt, κ_ijt); mean via tanh-half link on α^(TA)_0 + X^(TA)_ijt β^(TA) (incl. previous-frame turn angle, capturing directional persistence); concentration log κ_ijt = γ_0 + γ_1 s_ijt + w_j with ball-carrier random intercept w_j ~ N(0, τ²_w) — i.e., step length dictates turn concentration, and players differ in turn-angle variability.

**Plackett–Luce** (§2.3): for edge e of size k, P(Y_e = i_π(1)≻⋯≻i_π(k)) = ∏_{j=1}^{k−1} exp(u_{i_π(j)})/Σ_{ℓ=j}^k exp(u_{i_π(ℓ)}). Luce's choice axiom (IIA); latent-variable form X_i = u_i + ε_i, ε_i i.i.d. Gumbel(0,1), convenient for Bayesian inference.
**BT mixtures** (§2.4): P(Y_ij = i≻j) = Σ_{h=1}^H ω_h σ(u_i^{(h)} − u_j^{(h)}).

**Visualization inputs:** move sequence = ordered (x, y, limb) tuples, ~1,500 frames of 99 landmark features per frame.

**Match simulation:** goals scored by team i vs j follow a Poisson distribution P_ij(k) = (λ_ij^(f))^k exp(−λ_ij^(f))/k!, with expected goals λ_ij^(f) estimated as a quartic polynomial of Elo-derived win expectancy (least squares on ~40,000 national-team matches, separately for neutral and home/away; World Football Elo, home +100).
Poisson goal distribution: `P_ij(k) = (λ_ij^(f))^k exp(−λ_ij^(f)) / k!`.

Expected goals (neutral field, W_ij ≤ 0.9): `λ_ij^(n) = 3.90388·W_ij^4 − 0.58486·W_ij^3 − 2.98315·W_ij^2 + 3.13160·W_ij + 0.33193`; piecewise quartic for W_ij > 0.9 with large coefficients (308097.45501·(W_ij−0.9)^4 − … + 2.86899). Separate home/away quartics stated in full (Section 3.2).

**Data:** nflverse play-by-play + schedules 2020–2025 (six seasons, ~1,600 games). For each game, compute pre-game playoff-state for both teams from the actual season trajectory (use nflverse + a playoff-clinch simulator, or backfill from public clinch/elimination records): states = {alive, locked (seed clinched), eliminated, resting starters reported}.

Primal dynamic program for the informed player (P1): at each time step, P1 optimizes over mixed strategies via belief splitting, V(t, x, p) = Vex_p(min_u max_v E[...]) — convexification in the belief p; the dual dynamic program computes the conjugate value V*(t, p̂) used for the uninformed player's (P2's) strategy, p̂ ∈ ∂_p V.

P2's equilibrium strategy is derived via Blackwell (1956) approachability: keep the running average vector payoff (ξ_n, η_n) = (1/n Σ x_i, 1/n Σ y_i) inside the approachable set S = {ξ_n, η_n: (ξ_n, η_n) ≤ 6 − √3}; when g_n ∉ S, project onto the closest point c = argmin_{m∈C} ‖g_n − m‖ and play the mixed strategy q = (g_n − c)/‖g_n − c‖ ∈ Δ(K).

Constrained-game variant (Appendix I): collision-avoidance constraint c(x1,x2) = r − ‖(p_{x1},p_{y1}) − (p_{x2},p_{y2})‖_2, handled with a separately trained safety classifier ℱ: t × 𝒳 → ℝ (sub-zero level set = unsafe states) plus a γ·relu(−ℱ(t+τ, x^k)) penalty in the primal/dual minimax problems.
Hexner payoff: J(u1, u2) = E_θ[∫_0^T (‖u1‖²_R1 − ‖u2‖²_R2) dt + ‖x1(T) − zθ‖²_K1(T) − ‖x2(T) − zθ‖²_K2(T)], θ ∈ {−1, 1} is P1's private type.
1D reformulation payoff: J(t, θ̃1, θ̃2) = E_θ[∫_{τ=t}^T (θ̃1(τ) − θ)² d1(τ) − (θ̃2(τ) − θ)² d2(τ) dτ].
Critical reveal time: t_r = argmin_t ∫_0^t (d1(s) − d2(s)) ds; equilibrium θ̃1(s) = θ̃2(s) = 0 for s ∈ [0, t_r], θ̃1(s) = θ̃2(s) = θ for s ∈ (t_r, T] — i.e., conceal the type until t_r, then reveal.
Primal Hamiltonian: H(p) = 4p(1−p)(d1 − d2), with optimal Hamiltonian actions θ̃1 = θ̃2 = 1 − 2p.
Primal Bellman value: V(T_k, p) = 4p(1−p)D̃_k, where D_k = ∫_{T_k}^{T_{k+1}} (d1 − d2) ds and D̃_k accumulates negative-only mass backward.

Constrained primal (Eq. 77): min_{{u^k},{α_ki}} max_{{v^k}} Σ_{k=1}^I λ^k (V(t+τ, x^k, p^k) + τ E_{i∼p^k}[l_i(u^k, v^k)]) + γ·relu(−ℱ(t+τ, x^k)) s.t. u^k ∈ 𝒰, x^k = ODE(x, τ, u^k, v^k; f), v^k ∈ 𝒱, α_ki ∈ [0,1], Σ_k α_ki = 1, λ^k = Σ_i α_ki p[i], p^k[i] = α_ki p[i]/λ^k.
Constrained dual (Eq. 78): min over {v^k},{λ^k},{p̂^k} max over {u^k} of Σ_{k=1}^{I+1} λ^k V*(t+τ, x^k, p̂^k − τ l(u^k, v^k)) − γ·relu(−ℱ(t+τ, x^k)) s.t. Σ_k λ^k p̂^k = p̂, Σ_k λ^k = 1.

Beer-quiche primal value: V(0, ∅, p) = 5p_T/2 − 1 if p_T < 2/3, and p_T if p_T ≥ 2/3 (Cav of the max). At p_T = 1/3: Pr(u=Q|T) = 0, Pr(u=Q|W) = 3/4, Pr(u=B|T) = 1, Pr(u=B|W) = 1/4. Dual variable p̂ = [3/2, −1]^T; P2's equilibrium: if P1 picks beer, defer (d) and bully (b) with equal probability (λ1 = 1/2, λ2 + λ3 = 1/2); if P1 picks quiche, bully with probability 1.

Approximation/discretization theory: Theorem 3.1 — approximation error is linear in the time discretization, upper excess M(T − t0)τ. Theorem 4.2 — baseline complexity O(K³ C^{2K} I² ε^{−4} δ^{−2}). Appendix G, Theorem G.4: achieving prediction error δ at t=0 needs complexity at least O(T³ C^{2T} I² ε^{−4} δ^{−2}); error propagation bound ε_0^bias ≤ T C^T (ε^app + C(ε^minmax + ε^app)).
10-stage unconstrained Hexner game: CAMS estimates the target reveal time t_r = 0.60s ± 0.06s vs. ground truth 0.5s.

Data sampling for value networks: positions uniform in [-1,1]; velocities in [−v̄_t, v̄_t] with v̄_t = t × u_max; u_max = 12 both players (unconstrained); constrained: P1 u_{x_max} = 6, u_{y_max} = 12; P2 u_{x_max} = 6, u_{y_max} = 4; velocities normalized to [-1,1] during training; belief p uniform in [0,1].
Beer-quiche analytical equilibrium numbers: V(0,∅,[1/3,2/3]^T) = −1/6; dual p̂ = [3/2,−1]^T; P1's splitting points p^1 = [0,1]^T, p^2 = [2/3,1/3]^T with λ = 1/2 at p_T = 1/3.
